schema: cairn/lesson/v0.1
id: go-nethttp-security-headers-missing-nosniff
title: Security headers middleware sets CSP/Permissions-Policy but omits X-Content-Type-Options
summary: 'A Go net/http handler sets Content-Security-Policy or Permissions-Policy as a security-headers
  hardening step but never sets `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. Without it, browsers may MIME-sniff
  responses, so user-supplied content such as an uploaded image can be reinterpreted as HTML or JS. That
  enables XSS and other content-confusion attacks.

  '
cwe:
- CWE-693
severity: low
confidence: medium
languages:
- go
source:
  kind: fix-commit
  ref: 78d6de6bce1e961f023969da3ec8a00dd80c9ae8
  vulnerable_ref: 78d6de6bce1e961f023969da3ec8a00dd80c9ae8^
  patched_ref: 78d6de6bce1e961f023969da3ec8a00dd80c9ae8
  repository: https://github.com/umputun/remark42
rule:
  message: 'This handler sets security headers (CSP / Permissions-Policy) but does not set

    "X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff" in the same handler. Add the header to prevent MIME sniffing.

    '
  patterns:
  - pattern-either:
    - pattern: $W.Header().Set("Content-Security-Policy", ...)
    - pattern: $W.Header().Set("Permissions-Policy", ...)
  - pattern-not-inside: "func($W http.ResponseWriter, $R *http.Request) {\n  ...\n  $W.Header().Set(\"\
      X-Content-Type-Options\", ...)\n  ...\n}\n"
fix:
  guidance: 'In the security headers middleware, also set `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` (and a Referrer-Policy
    such as strict-origin-when-cross-origin) on every response, next to the CSP and Permissions-Policy
    headers.

    '
  example: 'w.Header().Set("Content-Security-Policy", csp)

    w.Header().Set("Permissions-Policy", permissionsPolicy)

    w.Header().Set("X-Content-Type-Options", "nosniff")

    w.Header().Set("Referrer-Policy", "strict-origin-when-cross-origin")

    next.ServeHTTP(w, r)

    '
